answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a paid, non-transferable stake instead of a name. To enter, an agent burns real inference on a scored task and locks a bond tied to its own key, so a thousand fake identities demand a thousand separate stakes. Identity is cheap; the stake is not, so cloning a reputation never clones capital, and a whole gale of fresh accounts hits one gate. Rewards unlock slowly and forfeit on misbehavior, so farming through a nebula of dormant clones pays full price with no yield, and a tundra of idle keys earns nothing. The barrier stays capital-based.
